title: Madlab - The Ultimate Innovation Hackathon
description: MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution. A Multidisciplinary Innovation Hackathon About the Opportunity MADLAB is a high-energy, multidisciplinary hackathon designed for individuals who dare to think differently, communicate confidently, build creatively, and execute ideas into practical solutions. The competition brings together software developers, marketing enthusiasts, sales strategists, business students, designers, and aspiring entrepreneurs to solve challenges through innovation, teamwork, and strategic thinking. This is not just a coding competition. Participants will be evaluated on their creativity, technical and practical skills, communication, problem-solving, marketing strategies, sales approach, and ability to present and execute ideas. Eligibility Criteria Open to college students and aspiring professionals with an interest in technology, business, marketing, sales, design, or entrepreneurship. Participants from all academic streams and specializations are welcome. Students from different colleges can form a team together (inter-college participation is allowed). Participants from different specializations can collaborate in the same team (inter-specialization participation is encouraged). No advanced coding experience is mandatory. Creativity, communication, business thinking, and execution matter just as much as technical skills. Participants must provide accurate registration details and follow the event organizers' instructions. Team Formation Participants may register individually or in teams of 2–5 members. Teams may include developers, marketers, sales representatives, designers, presenters, and business strategists. Each team should distribute responsibilities effectively and ensure that every member contributes. Each team must nominate one member as its primary point of contact. Team changes after registration require approval from the organizers. Competition Format and Rounds Round 1: The Spark — Problem-Solving and Ideation (30 minutes) Teams receive a problem statement and identify the problem, target audience, and potential solution. They must demonstrate original thinking, practical reasoning, and a clear understanding of the challenge. Round 2: The Build Lab — Creation and Strategy (90 minutes) Teams develop a working prototype, business concept, marketing campaign, sales strategy, or another relevant solution according to the assigned challenge. Developers can build prototypes, marketers can design campaigns, and sales-oriented participants can develop pitches and customer acquisition strategies. Round 3: The Pitch Arena — Presentation and Communication (5–7 minutes per team) Each team presents its solution to the judges, explaining the problem, proposed solution, target audience, implementation strategy, and expected impact. Teams must communicate their ideas clearly and confidently. Round 4: The Crossfire — Judges' Q&A (3–5 minutes per team) Judges question teams about their decisions, originality, feasibility, technical implementation, marketing approach, sales strategy, and scalability. Participants must demonstrate ownership of their work and respond professionally. Total estimated competition duration: 2.5–4 hours, depending on the number of teams and event scheduling. Problem Statements Participants will receive one assigned problem statement or challenge from the organizers. Challenges may cover the following areas: Technology and Development: Build a prototype, tool, website, application, or automation that solves a real-world problem. Marketing and Creativity: Develop a creative marketing campaign, brand strategy, social media concept, or customer engagement plan. Sales and Business Growth: Create a sales pitch, customer acquisition strategy, conversion plan, or business growth model. Communication and Innovation: Present an original idea, demonstrate persuasive communication, and turn a concept into an actionable solution. The final problem statement, required deliverables, and evaluation criteria will be communicated to participants before the relevant round begins. Evaluation Criteria Participants will be evaluated on the following criteria: Creativity and originality — 20% Problem-solving and practical execution — 20% Technical or domain-specific skills — 20% Communication and presentation — 15% Marketing, sales, and business thinking — 15% Teamwork, adaptability, and Q&A performance — 10% Judges' decisions will be final, subject to the event's published rules. Competition Rules All submissions must be created or substantially developed by the participating team during the competition, unless the organizers explicitly permit pre-existing resources. Pre-existing code, templates, AI tools, and third-party resources may be used only as permitted by the organizers. Teams must disclose significant external contributions. Plagiarism, copied submissions presented as original work, fabricated results, impersonation, and misrepresentation of contributions are prohibited. Every team member must contribute meaningfully to the competition. Participants must respect fellow competitors, judges, mentors, volunteers, and organizers. Teams must submit their deliverables before the announced deadline. Late submissions may be penalized or disqualified. Participants must not attempt unauthorized access to systems, misuse personal data, or engage in unethical or illegal activities. All presentations must be professional, relevant to the assigned challenge, and completed within the allocated time. Participants must follow the venue's safety requirements and the organizers' instructions throughout the event. Any disputes, rule violations, or exceptional circumstances will be reviewed by the organizing committee. Deliverables Each team must submit the relevant deliverables for its assigned challenge, which may include: A working prototype, demonstration, campaign concept, sales pitch, or business solution. A short explanation of the problem and the proposed solution. A presentation outlining the approach, target audience, execution plan, and expected impact. Supporting materials such as designs, mock-ups, code, campaign creatives, or a business model, where applicable. Final Note MADLAB is an opportunity to move beyond ideas and demonstrate what you can create, communicate, build, market, and sell. Whether you are a developer, marketer, salesperson, designer, or business thinker, your skills have a place in the lab. Bring your creativity. Challenge the ordinary. Execute the extraordinary. MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution. Note: The organizers should confirm the final team size, eligibility, round timings, problem statements, judging panel, submission process, and prizes before publishing the opportunity. Any details not yet finalized should be updated to reflect the actual event rules.

description: Innovate. Build. Disrupt.: SINGULARITY is a premier inter-college hybrid hackathon organized by BLITZ, the Computer Science Society of Keshav Mahavidyalaya, University of Delhi. Built for visionary thinkers, coders, and creators, this challenge invites students from colleges across India to collaborate, build, and pitch disruptive, real-world solutions across cutting-edge technology sectors. Registration Fee: 100 Rupee per member of the team For Payment check the SINGULARITY RULEBOOK, fill out the Google Form attached at the end of the ruleboook . Round 1: Online Evaluation: Teams must formulate their ideas and submit a conceptual presentation (PPT) detailing their proposed solution and implementation framework. A specialized faculty panel will evaluate the submissions and shortlist the most promising teams for the grand finale. Round 2: Grand Finale — On-Site Hackathon: The top 10 shortlisted teams will earn their spot in the Reading Room at Keshav Mahavidyalaya for an intense, single-day, in-person hacking and pitching experience. Teams will work on their solutions, demonstrate their innovations, and present their projects to the judging panel. Bring your laptops, choose your track, and prepare to design the technology of tomorrow! Themes & Focus Areas: Select one of the following seven tracks for your project: Cybersecurity: Protecting networks, ensuring data integrity, and securing digital infrastructure. FinTech: Engineering disruptive digital banking, payment solutions, and wealth-tech platforms. Healthcare: Empowering medicine, diagnostics, and patient care through technology. Robotics, IoT & Automation: Designing smart hardware, connected devices, and intelligent automated workflows. Web3: Building decentralized architectures, smart contracts, and blockchain-powered innovations. AR/VR & Immersive Experiences: Architecting virtual spaces and developing next-generation spatial computing interfaces. Open Innovation: Bring your own unique problem statement and develop a creative, technology-driven solution. Important Timelines: Registration Opens: 2 November 2026 Registration & PPT Submission Deadline: 10 November 2026 Round 1 Results: 13 November 2026 Final Offline Hackathon: 17 November 2026 | 9:00 AM – 5:30 PM Important: Ensure that your team completes registration and submits its PPT before the deadline to be considered for the first round. Prizes & Rewards: First Place: ₹5,000 Cash Prize + Goodies Second Place: ₹3,000 Cash Prize + Goodies Third Place: ₹2,000 Cash Prize + Goodies Perks For All Participants: All participants can look forward to event-branded goodies during the offline phase. Ready To Make Your Mark?: Bring your ideas to life, collaborate with brilliant minds, and compete to create solutions that matter. SINGULARITY 2026 — Where Ideas Converge and Innovation Begins. Organized By BLITZ | Computer Science Society | Keshav Mahavidyalaya, University Of Delhi
